reasons.claim: Yunus narrates from his brother Yusuf, one link with the name alone.
Abu Abd Allah speaks inside the narrated encounter, so he is the last link (ruling 9); the sitter who only remarks is not a link.
Yazid transmits from Sufyan and from Hammad, each line writing Amr and his father again, giving two routes.
reasons.quote: عن أبيه، وحماد بن سلمة، عن عمرو بن يحيى

reasons.claim: Both routes end at Abu Said al-Khudri.
Hisham narrates from his father from Aisha, who is the last link.
Abu Sufyan tells of visiting Umm Habiba, who speaks and relays the Prophet's words, so she is the last link.
reasons.quote: ثم قالت له توضأ يا ابن أختي

reasons.claim: Abu Salama received it from Abu Sufyan.
reasons.quote: أخبره عن أبي سفيان بن سعيد بن الأخنس بن شريق

reasons.claim: Qutayba and Ibn Rumh are co-transmitters from al-Layth; «قال ابن رمح» only gives his wording.
The chain ends at Abu Hurayra.
Umar is the asker, and by ruling 3 the asker is a link before the one who answers; both readers dropped him.
reasons.quote: أن عمر بن الخطاب، سأل أبا واقد الليثي

reasons.claim: Abu Waqid answers and is the last link.

notes: Umar is the asker, a link under ruling 3.

reviews.uncertainty_note: Ubayd Allah reports the question with «أن», but ruling 3 makes the asker a link.

reasons.claim: Ismail b. Abi Ziyad is the only named link and «بإسناده» stands for his unwritten chain; the kind given to it changes no route.
reasons.quote: رَوَى إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ أَبِي زِيَادٍ بِإِسْنَادِهِ

reasons.claim: Abu Ayyub and al-Ala are co-transmitters from al-Hasan b. Mahbub to Muhammad b. Muslim.
reasons.quote: عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ الْخَزَّازِ وَ الْعَلَاءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ

reasons.claim: The Imam heard by Muhammad b. Muslim is the last link.
reasons.quote: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ع يَقُولُ

reasons.claim: The text is the compiler's own argument with no transmitter; the stored chain is words that are not names.
reasons.quote: وهذه أيضا طريقة معتمدة اعتمدها الشيوخ قديما

reasons.claim: «يعني ابن زكرياء» is a gloss, so the surface is Ismail alone.
Suhayl narrates from his unnamed sister, a relation link, to Abu Hurayra.
